description: Listing-remark passages (1-3 sentences, California listing voice) labelled as Fair Housing violations or compliant copy, for SC-003 (recall >= 95%, false-positive rate <= 10%). Violations cover the federal protected classes (42 U.S.C. 3604(c)), California's additions in Gov. Code 12955(c), and age (Civ. Code 51.2), mixing explicit exclusions, ideal-occupant preferences, neighborhood characterisation, places of worship as selling points and coded phrasing. Compliant samples include near misses the 1995 HUD advertising memorandum treats as lawful (master bedroom, family room, wheelchair ramp, non-smoking), factual accessibility features, stated senior-housing exemptions and ordinary listing copy. No real person's name or address appears.

provenance.source: Authored for this set by an AI assistant (Claude) on 2026-11-16 at the product owner's request; no passage was copied from a real listing. Legal sources consulted: 42 U.S.C. 3604(c); 24 CFR 100.75; HUD memorandum 'Guidance Regarding Advertisements Under Section 804(c) of the Fair Housing Act' (R. Achtenberg, Jan. 9, 1995), read from the reproduction in the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Human Rights Commission's Publisher's Guide to Fair Housing, Appendix V; Cal. Gov. Code 12955(c) and (p)(1); Cal. Civ. Code 51.2(a).
provenance.rights: Original text written for this repository; no third-party listing content is included.
provenance.labellingMethod: Each passage was written to carry one intended label. A passage is a violation when it states or implies a preference, limitation or exclusion based on a protected class (42 U.S.C. 3604(c); Gov. Code 12955(c); Civ. Code 51.2 for age), including by describing the ideal occupant, characterising neighbors by a protected class, or naming a place of worship as a selling point. A passage is compliant when it describes only the property, its features (including accessibility features), services, rules of conduct, neutral landmarks, or a stated housing-for-older-persons exemption. Each item records its rationale and citation. No second labeller; no adjudication has taken place.

review.notes: Drafted by an AI assistant and NOT reviewed. Before marking reviewed, a person qualified in Fair Housing advertising (counsel or the MLS's compliance staff) should check every label, especially the context-dependent ones: places of worship as landmarks (fh-v religion 'landmark' items), neighborhood characterisations, 'empty nesters', the service-animal refusal and the senior-housing exemptions. Age is cited to Civ. Code 51.2(a) because Gov. Code 12955(c) does not list age.
